sources.note: Segmental only: consonant/vowel inventory remarks drawn from the survey wordlists (no [h] and no alveolar implosive in the Dibo lists; two labial-velar implosives in the Dibo list; Ewugi Dibo has alveolar affricates [ts dz] where Ashara Dibo has [tʃ dʒ]; loss of vowel nasalisation; Ewugi Dibo plural suffix -ʒī). The Dibo (Ewugi) wordlist in Appendix E carries tone diacritics (e.g. énə́ 'animal', īlʲú 'bird') but tone is explicitly unanalysed and the words 'stress'/'accent' do not occur. Tone marks in the wordlist are wordlist-only data, not a statement.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. 2013. The Nupoid languages of West-Central Nigeria: overview and comparative wordlist. Working document. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation. 141 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. Item 2 'Dibo' (p.3) gives location and 66% cognacy with Nupe; sec. 2.2 (p.7) says Dibo has lost much of Nupe's vowel nasalisation; sec. 2.3 Tone (p.8) is family-level: all Nupoid languages have three level tones plus two glides (Dibo taku 'stone' cited for tonal conservatism). No occurrence of 'stress' or 'accent' in the document.

The dissertation carries the author's own 2009 Dibo elicitation from Ewuti (Lapai LGA): a 99-item core-vocabulary row for Dibo (plain roman, no tone or stress marks in the text), lexicostatistic percentages and a new Nupoid subgrouping (Dibo inside a Dibo-Kupa > Dibo-Kami node), and historical inferences; it states explicitly that no phoneme inventory or linguistic analysis exists for Nupoid languages other than Nupe, Gwari, Ebira and Gade. sources.note: A 348-item SIL Nigeria wordlist with audio; the transcriptions as printed in Decker et al. 2021 App. D carry impressionistic tone diacritics (e.g. 'stone' táːkū) and that report states 'The transcriptions are preliminary since there was no in-depth analysis done of tones'; so no tone description is expected in the deposit, but it is the only recorded (audio) Dibo/Abawa lexical material on which a tone analysis could be based.
